title: Chapter 3 Quiz 16
description: Traps in every question. Follow each call to the end before you answer.
instructions: Chapter 3: Difficult: subprograms, recursion and traces.
Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: This recursive function should return N!. One line breaks it. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Function Fact(N) Returns integer
Begin
    If N = 0 Then
        Fact ← 1
    Else
        Fact ← N * Fact(N + 1)
    EndIf
End Function
questions.explanation: The call must use a smaller value to reach the base case N = 0. Watch out: with N + 1 the values grow and the function never stops.

questions.question: The recursive Fibonacci F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2), with F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1, is written without memoization. How many calls of F are made in total to compute F(5), counting the first call?
questions.explanation: Calls: c(0) = c(1) = 1, and c(n) = 1 + c(n-1) + c(n-2). That gives 1, 1, 3, 5, 9, 15. Watch out: we count calls, not the value of F(5). This is why memoization matters.
questions.hint: Count calls, not the value of F.

questions.question: How many multiplications are done when Fact(4) is computed with the recursive function (Fact(0) = 1 and Fact(N) = N × Fact(N - 1))?
questions.explanation: Fact(4) = 4 × Fact(3), Fact(3) = 3 × Fact(2), Fact(2) = 2 × Fact(1) and Fact(1) = 1 × Fact(0): 4 multiplications. Watch out: Fact(0) is a base case and does no multiplication.

questions.question: This function should return double its parameter. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Function Double(n) Returns integer
Begin
    Display(2 * n)
End Function
questions.explanation: A function must send its result back with Return. Watch out: Display shows the value on the screen, but the caller receives nothing.

questions.question: Fill in the value returned by each call of the recursive factorial.
questions.explanation: Fact(0) = 1, Fact(1) = 1 × 1 = 1, Fact(2) = 2 × 1 = 2, Fact(3) = 3 × 2 = 6, Fact(4) = 4 × 6 = 24. Watch out: Fact(1) is 1, not 0.

questions.question: Memoization changes the value that the Fibonacci function returns.
questions.explanation: Memoization only stores results so they are not recomputed. Watch out: it makes the function faster, but the values stay the same.

questions.question: Which subprogram should compute a value that the caller stores in a variable?
questions.explanation: Only a function returns a value. Watch out: a procedure can calculate and display, but it cannot give the value back.

questions.question: This should store the sum of r and 6 in r, then display it. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Function Sum(a, b) Returns integer
Begin
    Return a + b
End Function
Let r ← 4
Call Sum(r, 6)
Display(r)
questions.explanation: The result of a function must be stored with Let r ← Sum(r, 6). Watch out: Call Sum(r, 6) is allowed, but the result is lost, so Display(r) would still show 4.

questions.question: Put in order the steps of the recursive factorial for Fact(3).
questions.explanation: The calls go down to the base case first, then the returns come back up in the reverse order. Watch out: Fact(3) is the first to start and the last to finish.

questions.assertion: A recursive function without a base case ends quickly.
questions.reason: A recursive call keeps calling itself until a base case is reached.
questions.explanation: The assertion is false: with no base case the calls never stop. Watch out: the reason is true, and it is exactly why the function would never end.

questions.question: Sum(a, b) returns a + b. What does Sum(Sum(2, 3), Sum(4, 1)) return?
questions.explanation: The inner calls come first: Sum(2, 3) = 5 and Sum(4, 1) = 5, then Sum(5, 5) = 10. Watch out: the calls inside the brackets are evaluated before the outer call.
